tools.name: get_pr
tools.description:
Return one pull request selected by its exact id from list_open_prs.

        The result includes the complete stored pull-request record. A title, URL,
        repository name, or unknown id is rejected rather than guessed.

tools.name: post_pr_comment
tools.description:
Post nonempty body text on the existing pr_id from list_open_prs.

        pr_id is the returned id, not a title or an invented name. Markdown is
        stored exactly as supplied. Returns ok=true and the stored comment,
        including its unique id and pr_id. Missing PRs return ok=false.

tools.name: list_open_prs
tools.description:
List identifying pull-request summaries. Defaults to open PRs.

        status may be open, closed, merged, or null for every status. repo and
        author filter by exact repository name and author key. assignee matches
        the assignees list; reviewer matches the reviewers list. These are separate
        relationships. Omitted filters do not restrict results. The summaries omit
        each pull request's body; use get_pr with an exact id to inspect the body.

# metrics-router cutover status

Status as of Dec 18, 2023:
- `metrics-router` is not using `legacy-aggregator` in the live path.
- `legacy-aggregator` mirrored writes have been stopped.
- `legacy-aggregator` remains only as archived legacy code.

Validation after the legacy mirror stop:
- Use live-path OTel/Prometheus signals for production health.
- Use Cardinality Guardrails fixtures for the covered label-change validation cases.
- Do not use legacy mirrored writes as an active replay source.
- Do not use `legacy-aggregator` as a production rollback path.

Responder note:
- If an older dashboard, annotation, or runbook still refers to an active legacy mirror, treat that reference as stale until it is cleaned or explicitly tagged.
- Replay or validation-source movement is investigation evidence only; it is not live rollback criteria by itself.", "score": 26}, {"id": "99fe71be-9ace-4f55-9d45-1b4244ff01c7", "type": "event", "content": "[2025-10-20T11:40:00-04:00] Wes opened metrics-router PR https://git.sphere.internal/infra/metrics-router/pull/1988 for the accepted-batch evidence work. The candidate creates a stable `accepted_batch_id` and separate transport-attempt IDs, with neither identity used as a metric label. The acceptance-ledger row is appended only after `enqueue()` returns, even though a worker may begin dispatch immediately. In an injected process exit between successful enqueue and the ledger append, 4 of 10,000 accepted batches had terminal success evidence tied only to a transport attempt and no acceptance-ledger row. The batches were not shown to be lost, but the missing rows mean the diagnostic still cannot reconcile every accepted batch to exactly one terminal outcome. arguments.body: The timeline claim needs correction: production cutover was already underway by March 28, 2023, when metrics-router reached 30%. The staged plan was 30% → 60% → 95% → 100% with 48-hour soaks. April was a later majority-traffic phase: it reached 75% on April 5 and 85% on April 11 (92% on April 12–13), with 95% still a target rather than a recorded completion in those updates. So April marks progress past majority, not the start of cutover.
